newsitem.title: USA: Ford sees flat U.S. total '97 vehicle market.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees flat U.S. total '97 vehicle market.

text.p: Ford Motor Co chairman and chief executive officer Alex Trotman said Wednesday the automaker expects U.S. total vehicle sales for 1997 to be about flat with the 15.4 million expected for 1996.
Trotman, in the company's year-end presentation, said Ford expects total industry vehicle sales worldwide to be 52 million, up from 51 million expected for 1996.
"We're expecting some growth next year," Trotman said.
Trotman said Ford expects to report total 1996 revenues of $150 billion. The number two U.S. automaker had 1995 revenues of $137.1 billion.
Commenting on other markets, Ford predicted a flat market for western Europe in 1997 compared with the 14.2 million new vehicle sales seen there for 1996.

Trotman said South America and Asia/Pacific are expected to see the biggest worldwide market share growth between now and 2005. Those regions are expected to control 35 percent of the global market in 2005 compared to 19 percent now. By contrast, Trotman said Ford predicts North America and western Europe will fall to 50 percent of the global market versus 65 percent now.

Trotman said Ford is mounting a "all-out war" on costs in its European operations and expects the automaker to see an improved performance from that unit in 1997. He said the company is evaluating shrinking its capacity in Europe as part of those efforts but declined to discuss specifics.
